# Draft:Edward Boginsky

Edward Boginsky (born 1967, Chernivtsi, Ukraine) is a fine art and fashion printmaker based in New York City. He is notable for founding a high‑end print studio on Spring Street and for collaborating with fashion photographers and creative directors, helping shape the look of editorial publications and campaign imagery.
Early life and education
Boginsky was born in 1967 in Chernivtsi, Ukraine, into a family with a background in printing. After his family emigrated to the United States, he began working in his father’s print shop in New York City. By his late teens, he had developed a strong interest in fine art and fashion printing.
Career
In 1989, Boginsky founded a specialized fine art and fashion print studio in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, focusing on traditional and modern print techniques. His shop quickly became known for delivering high-fidelity prints to photographers, designers, and brands.
Artistic Collaborations
Boginsky collaborated on multiple look books and editorial projects alongside key creative figures including photographers Henry Leutwyler and Mark Havriliak, creative director Ruba Abu‑Nimah, and American Crew founder David Raccuglia. These projects often featured sophisticated duotone and tri‑tone printing that became signature visuals for fashion and grooming campaigns.
Legacy and impact
Boginsky is recognized for combining technical precision with creative innovation in print. His studio played a significant role in defining the visual identity of fashion-oriented look books and editorial series in the 1990s and early 2000s. While he later reduced public involvement and closed his Manhattan studio, his influence on print-based visual storytelling continues to be acknowledged by industry professionals.
